question: What is the order of the pedestrian intervals shown in Figure 4I-4, and what minimum durations are labeled for the first and last intervals?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 4I-4 shows the pedestrian intervals in the following order: the Walk Interval (steady WALKING PERSON), followed by the Pedestrian Change Interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND with countdown), followed by the Buffer Interval (steady UPRAISED HAND). The first interval (Walk Interval) is labeled "7 seconds MIN.," and the last interval (Buffer Interval) is labeled "2 seconds MIN." Standards (mandatory): - "A pedestrian change interval consisting of a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall begin immediately following the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication. Following the pedestrian change interval, a buffer interval consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement." - "The sum of the time of the pedestrian change interval and the buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time (see Paragraphs 7 through 16 of this Section). The buffer interval shall not begin later than the beginning of the red clearance interval, if used." - "All pedestrian signal heads used at crosswalks where the pedestrian change interval is more than 7 seconds shall include a pedestrian change interval countdown display in order to inform pedestrians of the number of seconds remaining in the pedestrian change interval." Options (permitted): - Per the figure notes: "The countdown display is optional for Pedestrian Change Intervals of 7 seconds or less"; "The Walk Interval may be reduced under some conditions (see Section 4I.06)"; and "The Buffer Interval, which shall always be provided and displayed, may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended." - "The additional time provided by an extended push button press to satisfy pedestrian clearance time needs may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 shows the sequence Walk Interval → Pedestrian Change Interval → Buffer Interval, with the Walk Interval labeled "7 seconds MIN.**", the Buffer Interval labeled "2 seconds MIN.", the calculated pedestrian clearance time spanning the change interval (and optionally the buffer), and the "Zero" point of the countdown display marked at the end of the pedestrian change interval. - [Image 2] Page 765 reproduces Figure 4I-4 in the context of Section 4I.06, showing the same interval order and the 7-second and 2-second minimum labels along with the relationships to associated vehicular phase intervals (G, Y, R). - [Image 3] Page 764 contains Figure 4I-3 (push button locations) and the Standard text of Section 4I.06 §4 requiring the change interval to follow the WALK indication and the 2-second minimum buffer interval. - [Image 4] Page 767 contains related Guidance and Support on walk interval timing at leading pedestrian interval locations but does not depict the figure itself. - [Image 5] Page 37 is a table of contents page listing "Figure 4I-4 Pedestrian Intervals" on page 724. Citations: - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Standard §4 (p.724) - Section 4I.04 Standard §1 (p.720) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725) - Page 765 - Page 764
gold_answer: Walk interval, pedestrian change interval, then buffer interval. The walk interval is labeled 7 seconds minimum and the buffer interval 2 seconds minimum, subject to the stated walk-interval exception.
